message.content:
**Answer**

There isn’t a named “species” that can be pointed to as the common ancestor of a lion (*Panthera leo*) and a zebra (*Equus quagga*).  
Both animals belong to the **super‑order Laurasiatheria**, so their most recent shared ancestor is the last common ancestor of that entire clade.

| Taxonomic level | Lion | Zebra |
|-----------------|------|-------|
| Kingdom | Animalia | Animalia |
| Phylum | Chordata | Chordata |
| Class | Mammalia | Mammalia |
| Infraclass | Eutheria | Eutheria |
| **Superorder** | **Laurasiatheria** | **Laurasiatheria** |
| Order | Carnivora | Perissodactyla |
| ... | ... | ... |

### When did this ancestor live?

- The last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria is estimated to have existed roughly **90–100 million years ago** during the Late Cretaceous period.  
- Fossil evidence suggests it was a small, insectivorous mammal that later diversified into the various lineages that make up modern carnivores, odd-toed ungulates, even-toed ungulates, bats, and whales.

### Why no specific name?

- The ancestor predates the fossil record for many of its descendant groups; it is inferred from phylogenetic analyses rather than directly observed fossils.  
- Because it is extinct and not represented by a single, well‑known species, scientists refer to it simply as the *last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria*.

---

**Bottom line:** The lion and zebra share a common ancestor at the level of the super‑order Laurasiatheria, an extinct lineage that dates back about 90 million years.

But likely they want the last common ancestor of the two species: the last common ancestor of the family Felidae and Equidae. That would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both. That is the last common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla? Actually, lion is in order Carnivora, suborder Feliformia. Zebra is in order Perissodactyla. The last common ancestor of those orders would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes both. That might be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes all artiodactyls? Zebra: Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Mammalia, Infraclass Eutheria, Superorder Laurasiatheria, Order Perissodactyla, Family Equidae, Genus Equus, Species quagga.

So both belong to superorder Laurasiatheria. So their last common ancestor is the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatheria. That would be the last common ancestor of the clade that includes Carnivora, Perissodactyla, Cetartiodactyla, Chiroptera, etc. So the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria. That ancestor would have lived around 90 million years ago. It was probably a small mammal. So answer: the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria.
